title: Unpaid household work is a multi-trillion-dollar social capacity that ordinary economic totals only partly show
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-107871 analysis of 2021–2024 American Time Use Survey and 2024 Current Population Survey wage data
geography: United States; nationally representative time-use and labor-market estimates

denominator.unit: national estimate of unpaid household work based on ATUS time and CPS wage proxies

daily_time.unit: hours per day spent on unpaid household work by most people

daily_replacement_value.unit: approximately dollars per day using selected wage proxies

national_annual_value.unit: 2024 dollars; estimated national market value of unpaid household work

women_share_of_workers.unit: percent of people doing unpaid household work, 2021–2024

women_population_share.unit: percent of U.S. population used as comparison, 2021–2024

care_burden_comparison.value: women and married people spent more time on childcare than men and unmarried people

later_outcomes.unit: care quality, exhaustion, pay, employment, health, household security, and political action

observations.method: GAO analysis of nationally representative ATUS data from 2021–2024 and 2024 CPS median hourly wages; replacement-value estimates use selected lower and higher wage proxies for types of unpaid work.
observations.uncertainty: The estimate depends on activity classification, time-diary reporting, wage proxies, and valuation choices. It does not measure emotional meaning, care quality, exhaustion, choice, household bargaining, or later outcomes.
observations.subgroup: People performing unpaid household work; demographic comparisons include sex, marital status, and childcare-related groups described by GAO.
observations.counterinterpretation: Replacement-cost accounting makes hidden work visible but cannot capture reciprocity, meaning, quality, or the possibility that households prefer some unpaid care; a large estimated value is not itself a welfare loss or a case for universal outsourcing.

boundary: This record estimates the time and replacement value of unpaid household work and reports selected demographic differences. It does not establish causal effects on poverty, gender inequality, health, wellbeing, labor supply, household bargaining, political action, or social welfare, and it does not follow the same household to later outcomes.
